thread.title: Is Apple iPhone X Production at Risk? - Barron's

author: Jon Swartz
title: Is Apple iPhone X Production at Risk? - Barron's
text:
Illustration: Getty Images JPMorgan Chase (ticker: JPM) expects a downturn in sales of Apple's (AAPL) iPhone X during the first half of 2018 -- and a new report suggests Asian markets are a major reason.
JPMorgan's dour look predicts steep declines in both iPhone X and overall iPhone unit shipments. For the first quarter, it expects iPhone X production of 15 million units, down 25% from its previous estimate. It gets worse in the second quarter: a 44% drop to 10 million units.
Overall iPhone shipments will slip to 52 million units in the first quarter, compared with past guidance of 55 million units, JPMorgan says. It predicts 42 million units shipped in the second quarter, down from 45 million units.
A major stumbling block for sales is Asia. According to a report in The Wall Street Journal, Apple is struggling in Asia, including China, India, Indonesia and elsewhere, as shoppers opt for less-expensive smartphones from Xiaomi , OPPO Electronics and Vivo.
The Chinese handset makers are developing high-end smartphones that compete directly with iPhone X, but don’t cost as much.
Meanwhile, a Piper Jaffray report concluded consumers want a bigger, cheaper iPhone. One could be on the way later this year, based on several reports of a forthcoming model called iPhone X SE .
